name: Grand Hyatt Baha Mar
insider_take: This ultra-luxe resort sits on Nassau's prestigious Cable Beach, where celebrity chef José Andrés operates multiple restaurants and the world's largest casino outside of Las Vegas draws high-rollers from around the globe.
whats_special: The Grand Hyatt anchors the massive $4.2 billion Baha Mar resort complex, featuring the Caribbean's longest lazy river at 1,000 feet, plus exclusive access to Robert Trent Jones Jr.'s championship golf course. The property showcases an impressive collection of over 7,000 pieces of Bahamian art, making it one of the world's largest hotel art collections.
pro_tip: Book treatments at the ESPA spa before 10 AM or after 4 PM for the most serene experience, and don't miss the rooftop pool's infinity edge overlooking Cable Beach – it's Instagram gold during golden hour.
dont_miss: The nightly Junkanoo performances in the resort plaza, swimming with dolphins at the adjacent Dolphin Cay, and dining at Katsuya for some of the Caribbean's finest Japanese cuisine. Cable Beach itself offers pristine white sand and calm turquoise waters perfect for water sports.
pros: World-class casino resort complex with access to Baha Mar's expansive amenities, including multiple pools, a water park, and a championship golf course
Stunning beachfront location on Cable Beach with direct access to one of Nassau's most beautiful stretches of white sand and turquoise water
Exceptional dining scene featuring over 40 restaurants, bars, and lounges across the Baha Mar resort campus
Exclusive Hyatt Privé booking benefits including complimentary breakfast, resort credits, room upgrades, and early check-in/late check-out when available
Lavish spa and wellness offerings at the ESPA at Baha Mar, one of the largest and most celebrated spas in the Caribbean
cons: Large-scale resort atmosphere may feel less intimate for guests seeking a quiet, boutique Caribbean escape
Premium pricing across dining, amenities, and resort fees reflects the luxury positioning of the property
Located away from downtown Nassau, requiring transportation for guests wishing to explore local culture and attractions
